steps.label: Make both terms sines
steps.margin_note: First mark. The identity needs two of the same function, so convert cos78° to sin12° using cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

recall.must_convey: That cos78° is converted to sin12°, so both terms are sines.
accept: cos seventy eight is sin twelve so both terms become sines

cos seventy eight ante sin twelve, rendu sines avthai

steps.why: The identity sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B)sin(A−B) needs both terms to be sines. Mixing a sine and a cosine matches no formula.
common_mistakes: Applying an identity to a mixed sin² − cos².

steps.label: Apply the identity and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B)sin(A−B) gives sin54°sin30°, and both of those are known exactly.

recall.must_convey: That sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B)sin(A−B) gives sin54° sin30° = (√5+1)/8.
accept: apply sin squared minus sin squared equals sin of the sum times sin of the difference to get sin fifty four sin thirty
sin fifty four is root five plus one over four and sin thirty is a half
the answer is root five plus one over eight
sin fifty four into sin thirty, root five plus one by eight

steps.why: The two angles were chosen so that their sum and difference are both standard angles — 54° and 30°. That is why an exact answer exists at all.
common_mistakes: Getting the sum and difference the wrong way round.
